questions.q:
Selecting from the given alternatives, fill in the blank in the following sentence with the correct idiom with the meaning 'to consider someone to be the most wonderful person in the world'.
I love my uncle very much. I think _____.
options: the sun rises and sets on him
the river originates and mixes on him
the day starts and ends with him
the sweets is made and eaten by him
questions.solution:
'The sun rises and sets on him' idiomatically places someone at the centre of your world — the most wonderful person, as the stem requires.

**Answer: the sun rises and sets on him**

questions.q: Choose the word that is the most appropriate synonym of the word "brisk".
questions.solution:
'Brisk' means quick, active and energetic.

**Answer: quick**

questions.q:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.

The project faced delays due to bureaucratic hurdles, lack of co-ordination, and the inconsistant approach of the contractors.
questions.solution:
'Inconsistant' is the misspelt word — the correct spelling is 'inconsistent'; the other words are fine.

**Answer: inconsistent**

questions.q: Choose the misspelt word from the given options.
questions.solution:
'Aberrasion' is misspelt; the correct word is 'abrasion'.

**Answer: Aberrasion**

questions.q: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to "understand".
questions.solution:
To 'misconstrue' is to misunderstand or interpret wrongly — the opposite of 'understand'.

**Answer: Misconstrue**

questions.q: The word "fair" is a homonym. In which sentence does it mean a public event with entertainment and stalls?
options: The judge gave a fair judgment in the case.
It's only fair that he gets another chance.
We enjoyed rides at the village fair last Sunday.
questions.solution:
Only 'We enjoyed rides at the village fair last Sunday' uses 'fair' as the noun meaning a public event with entertainment and stalls; the rest use it to mean just or light in colour.

**Answer: We enjoyed rides at the village fair last Sunday.**

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.
A false name used by an author instead of their real one.
questions.solution:
A pseudonym is a false or assumed name used by an author in place of the real one.

**Answer: Pseudonym**

questions.q:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

________ a permanent solution to their problems, the farmers may go on strike.
questions.solution:
'Failing a permanent solution' means 'in the absence of / if there is no', so it correctly introduces the farmers' conditional strike.

**Answer: Failing**

questions.q:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
They discovered a cure for the disease last year.
options: A cure for the disease will be discovered by them last year.
A cure for the disease is discovered by them last year.
A cure for the disease was discovered by them last year.
A cure for the disease has been discovered by them last year.
questions.solution:
The simple past active 'discovered' becomes the simple past passive: 'A cure for the disease was discovered by them last year.'

**Answer: A cure for the disease was discovered by them last year.**

questions.q:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
The play was being rehearsed by the drama group in the school auditorium.
options: The drama group rehearsed the play in the school auditorium.
The drama group is rehearsing the play in the school auditorium.
The drama group was rehearsing the play in the school auditorium.
The drama group has been rehearsing the play in the school auditorium.
questions.solution:
The past continuous passive 'was being rehearsed' becomes the past continuous active: 'The drama group was rehearsing the play in the school auditorium.'

**Answer: The drama group was rehearsing the play in the school auditorium.**

questions.q:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

Sanskriti is rather backward ______ her painting skills.
questions.solution:
'Backward in her painting skills' is the correct collocation for lagging in a skill area.

**Answer: in**

questions.q:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."

If I __would be laid off again__, I would seriously consider a career switch.
options: were to be laid off again
questions.solution:
The second conditional needs the subjunctive 'were': 'If I were to be laid off again, I would seriously consider a career switch.'

**Answer: were to be laid off again**

questions.q:
The following sentence is divided into four parts and are given in the alternatives A, B, C, and D. Select that alternative which contains that part of the sentence which has an error. Selecting the part with the error is the answer.
Our bicycles are fully equipped, with head and tail lights, gear shifts, a bell, and even a air pump.
options: tail lights, gear shifts, a bell,
questions.solution:
'A air pump' is wrong because 'air' begins with a vowel sound, so the error lies in 'and even a air pump' — it must be 'an air pump'.

**Answer: and even a air pump.**

questions.q:
In the sentence below, what is the function of the phrase "such as"?

"The skills acquired in these fields such as critical thinking, clear communication, close reading, and research are highly valued across many industries."
questions.solution:
'Such as' introduces examples of the skills just mentioned (critical thinking, communication, reading, research).

**Answer: To introduce examples**

questions.q:
"Graduates with a background in English literature or language often find fulfilling jobs in publishing, writing, editing, media, law, and digital marketing."

What type of verb is "find" in the sentence?
questions.solution:
'Find' takes the direct object 'fulfilling jobs', which makes it a transitive verb.

**Answer: Transitive verb**

questions.q: The word "polished" in the passage most nearly means _____
questions.solution:
Used of a person's skills, 'polished' means refined — improved to a high standard.

**Answer: improved to a high standard**

questions.q: What does the word "versatile" mean as used in the passage?
options: Able to adapt or be used in many ways
questions.solution:
As used in the passage, 'versatile' means able to adapt or be used in many different ways.

**Answer: Able to adapt or be used in many ways**

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Studying literature develops skills that have broad applications in many careers including publishing, writing, law, and digital media.
Literature and language degrees limit career options primarily to teaching.
Only writers and editors find good jobs after studying literature.
Careers in literature do not contribute much to society or the economy.
questions.solution:
The passage's main idea is that studying literature develops transferable skills with broad applications across careers such as publishing, writing, law and digital media.

**Answer: Studying literature develops skills that have broad applications in many careers including publishing, writing, law, and digital media.**
